copy.blurb:
Thursday 18 June 2026 at 22:00 UTC. Canada and Qatar on the card. On the Qatar side, the engine's number sits +20.0pp clear of the market — one of the widest in the priced field this far out from kickoff.

Elo has the two sides level: Canada on 1720, Qatar on 1720. With the prior even, the market price carries the weight of the disagreement. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Canada to win at 35%, the draw at 30%, and Qatar to win at 35%. The away side reads 35% on this distribution — the model's central case for Qatar.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Canada to win at 66%, the draw at 22%, and Qatar to win at 15%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Qatar side — 15% on the market, 35% on the engine, a +20.0pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Qatar side that lower bound is 30% — +15.2pp clear of the market's 15%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Qatar side.

News will move the prior. With kickoff 30 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +20.0pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +20.0pp gap across model and market on the Qatar side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Qatar at 35%; Polymarket sits at 15%.
copy.title: Canada v Qatar · the model leans Qatar
